sentences.t: Google has bought 1,700 acres for a data center at 22272 Charleston Road, at the north end of Buffalo, a town on the Kanawha River in Putnam County.

Governor Patrick Morrisey's office announced the purchase on Friday, March 27, 2026, three days after the Department of Commerce received Google's application for High Impact data center certification.
The certification was approved.
Google would not say what it paid or who sold the land, and the announcement gave no figure for the investment, the number of jobs, the emissions or the timing.
Morrisey called it "a strong signal that our state is competing and winning for the jobs and industries of the future."
The detail came later, in a federal permit application rather than a press release.
The project is called Avalon.
The filing describes eight data center buildings on the 1,699 acre site, more than 2.2 million square feet, with construction disturbing about 1,254 acres and more than 14 miles of internal road.
It would affect over 34 acres across 17 wetlands and more than 45,000 feet of 34 streams, and put 184 acres of spoil in the Kanawha River floodplain.
Two 30 inch intake pipes would be installed by horizontal directional drilling for the project's water treatment plant, with 850 feet of permanent impact along the Kanawha shoreline.
Nine federally protected species live in the range of the work, among them the Indiana bat, the northern long-eared bat, the tricolored bat, five freshwater mussels and the monarch butterfly.
Public comment on the Army Corps of Engineers permit closed on July 10, 2026, and Endangered Species Act consultation is waiting on biological surveys.
The state Department of Environmental Protection estimates West Virginia has already lost 80 to 90 percent of its wetlands.
Buffalo is not of one mind about it.

Chad Minamyer, who had brain cancer in 2012, said he wants out: "We don't know the long-term health effects of living near something like that. Who knows what might happen to some of these people 20, 30 years from now if they don't move away."

Mayor Conrad Cain said he was "tickled to death" and was waiting for more detail, while pointing out that the town now has Google to the north and Toyota to the south, the river on one side and a hillside on the other, and nowhere left to expand.
Delegate Kathie Hess Crouse said that if the project goes ahead it will be at least a year before construction begins.
The record carries no capacity figure for the site.
The 8,000 megawatt Monarch campus is proposed 33 kilometres away in Mason County, the only other data center project recorded within that distance.

Generation on this stretch of river is already heavy and mostly coal: John E Amos at 2,900 megawatts is 22 kilometres off, Kyger Creek 34 kilometres, Gavin at 2,722 megawatts 36 kilometres and Mountaineer 38 kilometres.
No moratorium or data center zoning limit is in force near the site.

unconfirmed: How much power the campus would draw, where it would come from, and how much water it would take from the Kanawha are not stated in anything found. The purchase price and the seller are undisclosed. No county or state hearing on the project has been reported.

sentences.t: The Ridgeline Facility would go between the towns of Thomas and Davis, in the corner of Tucker County that makes its living from Blackwater Falls and Canaan Valley.
Fundamental Data LLC wants to build a gas fired power plant there with diesel backup generators and send its output to a private data center on the same ground.
The electricity would not be sold to the regional grid, though state law now lets up to 10 percent of the generation be sold back.
How big it is depends on which document you read.
The West Virginia Highlands Conservancy describes a 785 megawatt gas plant.

POWER magazine, reading the filings in August 2026, describes about 800 megawatts of gas in a first phase and 3.1 gigawatts in a second, close to 1.3 gigawatts of solar, and fourteen data center buildings drawing over 2 gigawatts, with commercial operation targeted for 2028.
WV MetroNews reported the Wall Street Journal's account that the whole complex could cover nearly 10,000 acres across Tucker and Grant counties.
The record carries 1,656 megawatts and 10,000 acres, which matches none of those.
Large parts of the permit and its supporting documents were redacted, which is part of why the figures do not line up.
The public hearing was held at Canaan Valley Resort State Park, in Davis, on June 30, 2025.
More than 300 people came and between 100 and 150 of them spoke, so the hearing ran past its eight o'clock finish to midnight.
Davis Mayor Al Tomson said nobody spoke for it: "There were no people that said, 'Build the data plant because I want worse air quality.'"
At that point Fundamental Data held only an option on the land and said it was waiting to see whether the permit came through.
The permit, R13-3713, was issued on August 15, 2025, and Appalachian Mountain Advocates appealed it for Tucker United, the Highlands Conservancy and the Sierra Club.
A year later the appeal turned on whether the company had controlled the site at all on the day the permit was signed.

Appalachian Mountain Advocates, Tucker United and the Sierra Club raised the question, and the Division of Air Quality's director, Laura Crowder, opened an inquiry on July 31, 2026 and gave the company until August 7 to produce documents.
Fundamental Data handed over a redacted purchase and sale agreement dated July 19, 2024, between Western Pocahontas Properties and itself, for a 291 acre tract near Thomas.

On August 13, 2026 Crowder found the boundaries matched the permitted site and concluded the information was "sufficient to verify Fundamental Data LLC's legal site control at the time of permit issuance."

Casey Chapman of Fundamental Data defended the blacked out pages: "Private is not the same thing as secret. The economics and negotiated terms of a private land transaction have nothing to do with what comes out of a stack."
The finding settled the site control point and nothing else.
The project is proceeding under House Bill 2014, which took away the power of West Virginia communities to regulate high impact data centers.
Tucker United runs two campaigns against it: a petition asking the governor to veto the data center bill, and a letter drive against the air permit application.
This is the only data center site recorded in Tucker County.

What generates power around it now is wind and coal: the 66 megawatt Mountaineer Wind Energy Center 7 kilometres away, the 1,625 megawatt Mt Storm coal plant 20 kilometres, NedPower Mount Storm 25 kilometres and New Creek Wind 31 kilometres.

unconfirmed: The air permit's redactions mean the built capacity, the acreage and the diesel storage volume are not publicly settled, and the sources read give different figures. The status of the Air Quality Board appeal itself, as opposed to the site control inquiry, was not established. No tenant or customer is named anywhere. Whether the company has now bought the land beyond the 291 acre tract is unknown, and no home state for Fundamental Data LLC is given in the sources read.

sentences.t: Hog Lick Aggregates runs a quarry at White Hall, near Fairmont in Marion County, and is studying whether to put a microgrid and data center on it.
The study would use 300 acres to begin with, on land that could take at least 1,500, and at full build the company says the site could draw at least a gigawatt.
The record carries the site at 277 acres and 200 megawatts, which is the starting point rather than the ambition.
The idea the company leads with is cooling.
Rather than draw fresh water, it wants to run a geothermal loop through water in the abandoned coal mines under the property.

President Brian Redmond was careful about it: "We need to validate that. We need to study it. We need to understand it. But, if we can prove that that's a viable alternative, there are a lot of abandoned coal mines in West Virginia filled with water."
The company says Hope Gas and EQT can both run pipe to the site to supply the gas, which would have to be burned to get past the first phase.
Nothing is built and nothing is scheduled.
There is no timetable, and Hog Lick would have to sell the site or find a data center partner before anything could be built on it.
The company has said it remains open to proposals to develop the site for manufacturing or other commercial purposes instead.
Company officials have argued the site could support the NOAA supercomputing centre being assembled at the I-79 High Tech Park nearby.
Residents have already pushed back on the jobs claim, saying most of the work would be temporary construction and that a finished data center employs only a few hundred people.
That NOAA facility is two kilometres away, and it is one of the two data center sites recorded in Marion County.
The 1,954 megawatt Harrison Power Station is 11 kilometres from the quarry, the Grant Town coal plant 16 kilometres.
No moratorium or zoning limit on data centers applies nearby.

unconfirmed: No developer or tenant has been named and no application has been filed. The phase structure reported elsewhere as 150 megawatt steps could not be confirmed in a source that would open, and neither source read says what the quarry sells. The site prospectus in our record is a scanned PDF no text could be extracted from.

sentences.t: The Environmental Security Computing Center is a federal weather computer rather than a commercial data center, and it sits in the I-79 High Technology Park at Fairmont, in Marion County.
It collects and stores NOAA's climate and weather records, improves forecasting and tracks droughts, floods and wildfires.
In September 2024 NOAA said it would spend $100 million on a new machine for the site, named Rhea.

Jim Estep, president and chief executive of the West Virginia High Tech Foundation, said the park's expansion had been built in preparation for exactly this, and that Rhea "is going to help NOAA in their exploration of using artificial intelligence and machine learning to improve the weather, ocean and climate forecast and ecosystem modeling."
The record carries the $100 million cost and no capacity figure at all.
No opposition to the site has been reported.
It is on this map because the dataset counts high performance computing sites, not because anyone is fighting it.
Two kilometres away, the Hog Lick Aggregates quarry is being studied for a data center of up to a gigawatt, and its owners have argued the NOAA machine is a reason to build there.
The 1,954 megawatt Harrison Power Station is 13 kilometres off and the Grant Town coal plant 15 kilometres.

unconfirmed: The power draw, water use and footprint of the Rhea installation are not published in anything found, nor is the date it goes into service or the terms of NOAA's lease at the technology park. Our record names no operator for the site.

sentences.t: TransGas Development Systems wants a data center campus and its own gas plant at the Harless Industrial Park, off Twentytwo Mine Road at Holden in Logan County, West Virginia.

It is the second of two identical campuses the New York company has proposed in the southern coalfields, this one placed by the West Virginia Highlands Conservancy near the Mingo and Logan county line.
The Division of Air Quality approved air permits for both TransGas plants on October 2, 2025, after hearings in August and September at which dozens of residents spoke against them.
The conservancy reported 117 gas engines at each site, generating over 2,400 megawatts.
The Williamson Daily News put the machinery at 114 dual fuel gas and diesel engines, each over 28,000 horsepower.
The agency said both facilities "will meet all applicable state and federal air quality rules and regulations."
The record carries this site at 2,398 megawatts, the same figure as its twin.

The Ohio River Valley Institute read the filings as two campuses able to draw 2,457 megawatts each, together using more than 29.4 million megawatt hours a year against the 33 million the whole state uses, and burning 218 billion cubic feet of gas to do it.
The plants would be off grid, built for the campuses alone, supplying nobody else in West Virginia.
TransGas has said it wants to take data center capacity to 9.8 gigawatts.
On December 3, 2025 ten Mingo County residents sued over the whole Adams Fork project in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia, case 3:25-cv-1013.

They named TransGas along with the Huntington District of the Army Corps of Engineers, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, and alleged breaches of the Endangered Species Act, the Clean Water Act, the National Environmental Policy Act and the Natural Gas Act, citing the endangered Guyandotte and Big Sandy crayfish.
On December 23, 2025 Judge Robert C. Chambers refused to halt the project while the case runs.
The twin campus at the former Twisted Gun Golf Course is 22 kilometres away.
Nothing near this size generates power around here: the closest plants on record are an 111 megawatt solar project 31 kilometres off and the 260 megawatt Big Sandy gas plant 64 kilometres off.
No moratorium applies.
The organised opposition here runs through the West Virginia Citizen Action Group.

unconfirmed: Reporting on Adams Fork treats the two sites together, so almost nothing is specific to Harless: its acreage, its water supply, its tenant and its construction schedule are all unstated. Our record files the project in Mingo County, but the address it gives, off Twentytwo Mine Road at Holden, is in Logan County. Sources disagree on whether there are 114 or 117 engines.

sentences.t: Alpha Technologies is converting the former Appalachian Power office at 1125 6th Avenue in downtown Huntington, in Cabell County, into a data center.
The 60,000 square foot conversion was put at $10 million, announced on October 30, 2024, with work expected to begin early in 2025 and about 30 people employed at the finished site.
Alpha Technologies runs from South Carolina and hosts data services for governments, businesses and health care providers.
It said the centre would help bring high speed fibre to the area and give customers a choice of internet provider.
The record has it under construction and holds no capacity figure.
No opposition to it has been reported.
A conversion inside an existing downtown block is not the kind of project that brings people to a council meeting, and the pressure in this corner of the state is elsewhere.
Across the river in Ohio, Ironton put a moratorium on data centers on February 12, 2026, and Boyd County in Kentucky followed on July 9, 2026.
Within 40 kilometres the record holds the proposed 2,000 megawatt Rubix data center 22 kilometres away, TeraWulf's 285 acre Muskie site at Ashland 31 kilometres, and the Ravel project 34 kilometres.
This one is the only data center site recorded in Cabell County.
The gas plants nearby are modest by the standards of this list: Ceredo at 450 megawatts is 10 kilometres away and the Big Sandy Peaker 300 megawatts at 16 kilometres.

unconfirmed: Whether the conversion was finished, and when, could not be established: the announcement said early 2025, and nothing later than that announcement and its reprints was found. The power draw, the cooling method and whether the building has taken on tenants are all unstated.

sentences.t: The QTS data center campus at Kearneysville straddles the Jefferson and Berkeley county line, and almost everything approved so far is on the Berkeley side.
The F.O. Day Company sold three parcels, about 300 acres in all, to IB10 Martinsburg LLC in July 2024, and QTS, a data center developer based in Overland Park, Kansas, is running the development.
Of that land, 90 acres lie in Berkeley County, with a narrow access strip off Charles Town Road, and 191 acres lie in Jefferson County, already zoned industrial.
The Berkeley County Planning Commission approved the concept plan for the Berkeley parcels in March 2025.

That plan covers two data center buildings, a guard shack, an electrical switching station, a water tank and several stormwater retention ponds, with water and sewer for the first phase coming from Berkeley County.
The Jefferson County planning office has received nothing to review.
A QTS representative said only: "We are in the initial stages of planning. We look forward to expanding our footprint in West Virginia to meet growing demand from our customers in the market."
The record files the project in Jefferson County at 90 acres, which is the acreage of the Berkeley half.
This site sits at the western edge of the Northern Virginia data center belt, and the crowding shows in what is around it.

Ten other data center projects fall within 40 kilometres, among them Penzance's 600 megawatt campus 21 kilometres off, CyrusOne Shaw Road at 31 kilometres, Amazon's BWI site and Quantum Frederick Park at 33 kilometres, and Microsoft and Google sites at Leesburg 35 and 37 kilometres away.
Frederick County, Maryland, brought in zoning limits on data centers on July 1, 2026.
Generation close by is thin for that load: an 80 megawatt solar plant 8 kilometres away, then the 299 megawatt Dickerson gas plant at 36 kilometres.

unconfirmed: No megawatt figure has been published for the campus and our record holds none. There is no announced investment, construction schedule, building count for the Jefferson County parcel, or water withdrawal figure. No public hearing or organised opposition was found in Jefferson or Berkeley County.

sentences.t: Penzance Management, a real estate developer, plans a $4 billion data center campus on 548 acres in the Falling Waters district of Berkeley County, north of Martinsburg.
The state announced it on March 9, 2026.
At full build the campus would run to about 1.9 million square feet and 600 megawatts of IT capacity.
The state says it would take more than 1,000 construction workers and leave at least 125 full time jobs.
It is the first project to be given West Virginia's new High Impact Intelligence Center designation.
Governor Patrick Morrisey called the investment "a historic win that proves West Virginia can compete at the highest level for the global tech economy."
The record carries the same 548 acres, the same $4 billion and the same 600 megawatts.

The eastern panhandle is where West Virginia's data center growth is concentrated, close enough to Northern Virginia to serve that market, and the nearest comparable project on record is the QTS campus at Kearneysville, 21 kilometres away.
Frederick County in Maryland, 40 kilometres off, wrote zoning limits on data centers on July 1, 2026.
Local generation is small and mostly solar: an 80 megawatt plant 30 kilometres away, a 150 megawatt plant 42 kilometres, and a 100 megawatt gas plant at Chambersburg the same distance.
Six hundred megawatts would be several times the nearest generation, so the power has to come from the wider PJM grid, whose peak load is 144,530 megawatts.

unconfirmed: No tenant is named and no construction date is given. Water supply, cooling method, backup generation and the interconnection arrangement are all unstated. No independent local reporting on the site, no county filing and no resident comment was found, so the account here rests on the state's own announcement. The Data Center Dynamics report our record cites could not be fetched.

sentences.t: The National Energy Technology Laboratory has run computers at 3610 Collins Ferry Road in Morgantown, in Monongalia County, for years, and is building one room to hold the data centers now spread across its campus.
The Computational Science and Engineering Center, under construction as of May 22, 2025, is 14,000 square feet, and the laboratory calls it its largest construction project in more than a decade.
It will pull those existing data centers into a single facility, with a server hall for the laboratory's supercomputer, Joule, a visualisation centre and collaboration space.

The part that sets it apart is the room left for a Cerebras wafer-scale engine, a supercomputer reduced to one chip, which the laboratory describes as the largest single computer chip produced in the world to date.
It claims 470 times faster processing than traditional resources for the work it suits, which would take a research model that runs for about a year down to less than a day, on far less energy.
The entry holds no capacity figure and 50 acres, which is the laboratory campus rather than the building.
This is a federal research site, and no opposition to it has been reported.
What is around it is another matter.
Project Hummingbird, a 1,000 megawatt proposal, is 18 kilometres away, the NOAA computing centre at Fairmont 33 kilometres and the Hog Lick quarry study 35 kilometres.
Morgantown is ringed by coal plants: the Morgantown Energy Facility 4 kilometres off, Longview at 710 megawatts also 4 kilometres, and the 1,098 megawatt Fort Martin station 6 kilometres.
Over the Pennsylvania line, South Strabane wrote zoning limits on data centers on February 4, 2026.

unconfirmed: The cost of the building and its completion date are not published in the laboratory's own announcement, and its power draw and cooling are not stated. Whether the West Virginia Public Broadcasting report our record cites, about the lab hosting an AI data center, describes this building or a separate arrangement was not resolved.

sentences.t: The Monarch data center campus takes in up to 2,250 acres north of Point Pleasant in Mason County, between the Ohio River, the CSX tracks and Route 62.
It began as Fidelis New Energy's Mountaineer GigaSystem, became a data center campus called Monarch, and has changed hands since.

On Monday, March 16, 2026, Nscale Global Holdings, a British company backed by Nvidia, Nokia and Dell, bought American Intelligence and Power Corp, the developer of the campus, which Fidelis New Energy and 8090 Industries had sponsored.
Nscale announced a letter of intent with Microsoft the same day to supply 1.35 gigawatts of AI compute on Nvidia Vera Rubin hardware.
The first phase is 2 gigawatts, with equipment installed across 2026 and 2027 and the campus running in the first half of 2028.
Full build is put at 8 to 10 gigawatts; for scale, the John E Amos coal plant is 2.9 gigawatts.

The power is generated behind the meter: 2 gigawatts of fast response gas generator sets ordered from Caterpillar, delivered between September 2026 and August 2027, with batteries to absorb the swings an AI load makes.
A 30 mile, 24 inch gas pipeline from Hope Gas, costing $250 million, will feed it.
Cooling water comes from the Ohio River.
The company says it will sequester carbon to offset the emissions, and that the design uses less water with no effect on municipal supply or residential users.

It expects to employ upward of 2,800 people, and Marshall University and Mountwest Community and Technical College have signed a training and apprenticeship agreement meant to give Mason County residents first call on the engineering and facilities jobs.
Nscale's chief executive, Josh Payne, said: "We build where the energy is, and we invest deeply in the communities that welcome us," promising quality jobs and long-term opportunity.
The permit filings describe a 2.16 gigawatt gas plant with 864 reciprocating engines powering three data centers.
The Environmental Integrity Project ranked it second in the country for estimated greenhouse gas emissions among planned data center gas plants.
Projected annual emissions are 1,043 tons of carbon monoxide, 900 tons of volatile organic compounds, 506 tons of nitrogen oxides and 38 tons of fine particulate matter.

Earthmoving has already gone wrong four times on the record: state inspectors cited the site on May 24, May 28, June 4 and June 10, 2026 for a silt fence that separated, sediment laden water discharging into the Route 62 culvert, a missing section of perimeter control and mass earthwork done earlier than approved, and sediment left in an unnamed tributary.
Flooding over the weekend of May 23 and 24 reached about half a dozen Mason County residents, with damage mainly to garages, crawlspaces and heating and air conditioning equipment.
The West Virginia Economic Development Authority approved a $62.5 million forgivable loan for the project in 2023, of which $25 million has been paid out.
About 60 people met in Point Pleasant on Tuesday, March 17, 2026 to work out what they could do.
West Virginia Citizen Action, the West Virginia Rivers Coalition and Fair Shake Environmental Legal Services put the meeting on.

Morgan King, climate and energy program manager at WV CAG, told them the plant would need five million gallons of water a day, about what the city of Charleston uses, and that House Bill 2014 had stripped away the county's power to regulate it.

Mike Wooten, from Camp Conley next to the site, said he was not totally against it but wanted protection: "I want to be protected by the people [who are] supposed to protect me, which is, you know, the governor, our legislators, [the] EPA, the permit process. Let's not circumvent or cut things off so we can bring these plants in."
Elaine Matheny, of Point Pleasant, offered to help organise, and told residents to read up on data centers built elsewhere.

King's advice was to watch the public notices for each construction stage, and she put it plainly: "You fight big corporations by building power in communities and by building up with numbers. That comes back to the organizing, getting together, talking with your neighbors."
The record carries the project at 8,000 megawatts, 2,250 acres and $5 billion, and names the developer as Fidelis and Nscale together.
The nearest generation is on top of it: Kyger Creek at 963 megawatts and Gavin at 2,722 megawatts are both 2 kilometres away, and Mountaineer at 1,299 megawatts is 17 kilometres.
Google's 1,700 acre Buffalo site is 33 kilometres upriver.
No moratorium applies, and under House Bill 2014 the county could not impose one.

unconfirmed: The carbon sequestration the company says will offset its emissions has no named site, permit or volume in anything read. Whether the $62.5 million loan follows the project to its new owner was not established. The five million gallons a day figure comes from an advocacy group reading the filings, and the withdrawal permit itself was not seen. Air permit issue dates for the 864 engine plant were not established. The Mountaineer GigaSystem was described here as a hydrogen plant with carbon capture and a biomass power station, which the cited report does not say, so that description has come out.
